title: Decompose batcher control plane and introduce explicit prefetch contract
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months the continuous batcher control plane and KV cache have accreted behaviour: ad-hoc prefetch calls embedded in the batcher loop, eviction side-effects in the fast path, and tightly coupled telemetry. This makes it hard to reason about tail latency, complicates rolling changes to prefetch heuristics, and increases risk during dependency upgrades (libaio/libuv) and scheduler changes.

Goal: Separate concerns by extracting a minimal, well-documented prefetch contract and a lightweight control-plane facade so the batcher core can focus on aggregation/dispatch. The prefetch contract will own warmup + KV prime semantics, run in a bounded async worker pool, and expose deterministic hooks for admission and backpressure. The control-plane facade will coordinate slot leases, optional prefetch intent annotation, and emit standardized telemetry labels.

Non-goals: This ticket does not redesign the allocator or change model-routing policies; it does not replace the KV store implementation. It does aim to make future allocator or KV backend swaps lower-risk by reducing coupling.

Deliverables: (1) Prefetch contract interface and in-process worker implementation with feature flag. (2) Control-plane facade that exposes: RequestIntent, LeaseAcquire, LeaseRelease, PrefetchHint APIs. (3) Integration tests for deterministic prefetch + eviction ordering. (4) New telemetry shim with per-lease labels and histogram buckets for prefetch latency. (5) Migration guide for toggling feature flag and rolling back.

Constraints: Must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments. Must not add >5ms median tail to 99.9p under 95th percentile load when feature-flag disabled. Runtime dependency upgrades required: bump libaio and metrics client; will be staged in a companion PR.
acceptance_criteria: Batcher core no longer calls KV warmup directly; warmup happens through prefetch worker when feature flag on
End-to-end tests that verify prefetch ordering and that eviction does not remove in-flight prefixes within the same epoch
No regression in 99th/99.9th latency (<= 3% change) measured on canary cluster with 48h smoke
Telemetry emits prefetched=true label when prefetch was used and includes prefetch_latency_ms histogram
Controlled rollout steps and documented rollback path in runtime-2026.04 release notes
rollout_plan: Deploy to internal staging (canary-hosted) and run synthetic traffic for 24h
Enable in low-traffic Dedicated pool for 12h and monitor prefetch success ratio, eviction churn, and 99.9p latency
Gradual ramp to 30% of capacity over 48h if metrics stable, then full rollout next week
If rollback required: flip feature flag off and run eviction sanity checks; follow documented rollback checklist
mitigation_plan: If prefetch worker memory or CPU causes regressions, throttle worker pool dynamically by circuit-breaker and fall back to legacy inline warmup. Add guard rails to keep worker pool capped per-GPU. If telemetry shows unexpected eviction churn, pause rollout and revert prefetch to 'intent-only' mode (hints without actual warmup) while we investigate.
notes: Design doc: drive/Redwood/runtime/prefetch-contract-v2 (link in PR) - prototype sketches and sequence diagrams
Related infra work to schedule: small upgrade to libaio in agent image (tracked in infra-ops ticket)
We will reuse existing lease-heartbeat flows; facade keeps a thin shim to avoid race windows seen in ENG-26109
